questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go somewhere where English was the primary language and that I wanted to go to a university that was widely known and respected. And also, I had been to Dublin before and I knew I loved the culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A little diffictult, Trinity's Erasmus department is not the most informative and you often have to reach out to them in order to attain information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a bus pick up service at the airports provided by Trinity which I used and I was dropped off at my accommodation. But other than that the assistance was limited, which I found to be fine though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Rent in Dublin is incredibly expensive and it is very hard to find a place to live. I was so lucky that I had read another of these reviews that recommended the private accommodation Binary Hub, which is where I chose to live. I loved it there and made most of my friends there. I would definitely recommend living in a private accommodation like Binary Hub (this one is owned by the company aparto – they have other accomodations in Dublin as well). But be quick to sign up, the rooms fill up early. 

I had a room with my own toilet and shower and then I shared a kitchen with four other people. It was lovely and a very social place with both Irish people, Erasmus students, and other foreign students who were doing their entire degree in Dublin.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to live off campus see if you can still find somewhere close to Trinity. I loved that my accommodation was in walking distance (20 mins) from Trinity and the city center. And if you wanna maximise the amount of people you meet, find an accommodation that is like a dorm/kollegie (such as Binary Hub). There is always a party or something social going on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A quite frustrating process, the Academic Registry is very very slow. I - like all other students - couldn't sign up for my classes until the end of the week before the classes started - so different than KU. But that is how it is every year in Trinity it seems. Yet, everything worked out just fine in the end, so there wasn't anything to worry about.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The week before classes start you can begin to register for modules. The registration completely online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can email your department or Academic Registry and they are normally pretty fast to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the modules I wanted. It does not seem like the classes can fill up in the same way they do at KU, so in my experience you can expect to get all the classes you want (as long as the classes are available to you as an Erasmus student).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ultra-patient and a little proactive, Trinity is not super good at informative when it comes to registration up until the time you need to register. But for me it all worked out even though the process was a little frustrating. So just be patient.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my modules were BA-level. I would say the level was similar to courses at KU or a little lower. Similar amount of reading but the exams were so much less time consuming. Three of my exams consisted of take home essays and one of them was an online "exam" where I had to answer three questions in two hours (open book). But you can just choose to sign up to modules that have an exam form you feel comfortable with. Looking back I probably wish I had only chosen modules with take home exams so I would have been done with my exams earlier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty different, but in a nice way. At Trinity I had a 45 min lecture and a 45 min tutorial with a professor and a small amount of people from the class every week. So a lot more time to talk and discuss with the professor than at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Globalisation and Development
Poverty and Policy in a Global Context
Labour Markets, Gender and Insitutions
Conflict Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of my classes, but I especially enjoyed Globalisation and Development. Also Conflict Studies was a great way to learn about Northern Ireland and the troubles.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Non.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The price of food, going out to eat and going to drink at pubs is much lower in Dublin.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have every single club/society and sport available you could imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely join a society, there are so many to choose from and they all offer fun activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Howth is great a very close to the city. But just go to as many pubs as possible with your friends, those were some of my favorite moments of my exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Irish people are so kind and welcoming. The social barrier is small because their drinking culture is pretty similar to the Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in private accommodation/uni accommodation instead of living in an apartment with other exchange students. Sign up for societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture. It is just amazing and unique to Ireland.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Book you accommodation as early as possible. 
- Be patient with the module registration, it will work out even though it can seem slow.
- In my experience it was not that difficult to get good grades, so remember you only need to pass the classes and enjoy your time going to pubs and being with friends instead of studying all day long. The exchange is over so soon so enjoy every moment you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Explore the campus, it is beautiful and historic.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Becoming very trustful of my academic skills and knowing the level taught at KU is very high.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Perhaps knowing how much time I had to put into studying because it was hard to know what level the professors expected since it was my first time taking classes there. But I was positively surprised at how low the expectations were.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
